program_name: Management (Laurea Magistrale) — Green Economy and Sustainability curriculum (English-taught curriculum inside the Management LM, University of Brescia). NOTE: this record describes the Green Economy and Sustainability curriculum specifically, not the whole Management LM, which also contains a second English curriculum (International Business) and several Italian-taught curricula.
teaching_language: English (this curriculum). The Management LM as a whole is a mixed-language degree: two curricula are delivered in English — 'Green Economy and Sustainability' and 'International Business' — while the remaining curricula (e.g. Business finance / Corporate finance, Marketing, Production and Logistics, Management Control, Professional Practice, Sustainability) are delivered in Italian. Indexed UNIBS text states that for students enrolled in the Green Economy and Sustainability and International Business curricula the language-skills requirement refers to English.
campus: Brescia — Department of Economics and Management (Dipartimento di Economia e Management). Teaching/student administration reference address given by UNIBS: U.O.C.C. Segreterie Studenti, Via S. Faustino 74/B, 25121 Brescia. [uncertain] The exact teaching building for this curriculum (the Economics area also uses the Contrada Santa Chiara premises) could not be confirmed because the official page could not be opened directly.
degree_class: LM-77 — Scienze economico-aziendali (Management). Confirmed via search-engine indexed UNIBS content describing 'The LM-77 Management degree' with the Green Economy and Sustainability and International Business English curricula. [uncertain] — not read directly from the official page.
english_delivery_scope: english_curriculum_within_italian_programme — The degree programme 'Management' (LM-77) is a single Italian degree course that contains multiple curricula. Only two curricula are taught in English: 'Green Economy and Sustainability' (this record) and 'International Business'. A student must specifically select the Green Economy and Sustainability curriculum to receive English-medium instruction; enrolling in 'Management' generically does not guarantee English delivery. Indexed course-content evidence for this curriculum shows English-titled units across both years (Year 1: Business Contract Law 6 CFU, Business History 9 CFU, Corporate Social Responsibility and Sustainability 9 CFU, Environmental Economics 9 CFU, Financial Statement Analysis 9 CFU, Organizational Behavior 6 CFU, plus 12 CFU free-choice electives = 60 CFU; Year 2: Financial Management 6 CFU, Advanced Marketing 6 CFU, Methods and Models for Environmental Sustainability 9 CFU, Supply Chain and Logistics Management 12 CFU, Resource and Energy Economics 9 CFU, Green Logistics Lab 2 CFU). Total 120 CFU over two years.
programme_status: active_first_year — The curriculum is presented by UNIBS as an active, recruiting English-taught curriculum of the Management LM, and it appears in the 2026/2027 admissions cycle for Economics-area master's degrees. No phase-out or suspension notice was found in indexed UNIBS content. [uncertain] — official 2026/2027 course page could not be opened directly to confirm first-year activation for AY 2026/2027 specifically.
pre_evaluation_required: Yes, for candidates holding a foreign qualification. UNIBS states that for open-access master's degrees in the Economics, Engineering and Law areas, pre-evaluation by the relevant Commission is compulsory for candidates with foreign degrees, in order to verify curricular requirements and personal preparation. Platform: PICA (online procedure) at https://www.unibs.it/en/international/degree-seeking-students/admission/pre-evaluation-masters-degrees. A EUR 20 fee is payable at the end of the online procedure. For AY 2026/2027 the non-EU pre-assessment round is open until 15 March 2026 (noon, Italian time), with outcomes communicated by email around mid-May 2026. EU and EU-equivalent citizens holding a foreign undergraduate qualification apply through a separate, later pre-assessment window (for AY 2025/2026 that window ran 30 June – 21 July 2025). [uncertain] — the exact EU pre-assessment window for AY 2026/2027 was not found.
entry_test_name: There is no external standardised admission test (no TOLC, no SAT) for this curriculum. Where the candidate does not qualify for direct admission, UNIBS applies an internal admission test (colloquio/prova di ammissione) set by the Management degree course Commission, covering the content of specified subjects; the syllabus and bibliography for the test are published as a downloadable file on the Management enrolling page. As an alternative route to demonstrating adequate personal preparation, UNIBS accepts the GMAT (Graduate Management Admission Test) with a total score of not less than 600/800. This internal test is selective in the sense that it gates admission — it is not merely orientative. [uncertain] — exact test format (written/oral), number of sessions and dates could not be verified directly.
admission_type: Open access / unrestricted access (accesso libero), with mandatory verification of curricular requirements and personal preparation. UNIBS states that second-cycle degrees run by the Department of Economics and Management are open access with no cap on enrolment numbers, but that registration is subject to assessment of the candidate's academic career. There is therefore no numerus clausus and no ranking list, but admission is not automatic: a candidate who does not meet the direct-admission thresholds must sit the internal admission test.
academic_requirements: 1) A bachelor's degree (Italian laurea or a foreign qualification recognised as suitable) is required. 2) Minimum curricular requirements: a minimum number of CFU must have been earned in specified disciplinary areas / scientific-disciplinary sectors (SSD) as set out in the Management course Academic Regulations (Regolamento didattico); UNIBS applies a tolerance of 6 credits on the verification of the minimum curricular requirements, provided the relevant specific disciplinary field is still present in the candidate's career. 3) Direct admission on grade: for candidates with a degree obtained abroad, the Commission deems personal preparation achieved where the bachelor's final mark is at least 85/110 in the Italian scale, or equivalently at least 77/100. 4) Alternative personal-preparation routes: a weighted average of examinations of not less than 23/30, or a GMAT total score of not less than 600/800. 5) Candidates who meet none of these thresholds must pass the internal admission test. [uncertain] — the exact SSD list and per-sector CFU minima (e.g. SECS-P/07, SECS-P/08, SECS-P/01, SECS-S/06, IUS/) could not be retrieved because neither the enrolling page nor the Regolamento didattico PDF could be opened. Admission requirements appear to be defined at the level of the whole Management LM and therefore appear to be identical for the Green Economy and Sustainability curriculum and the International Business curriculum; no curriculum-specific differentiation was found in indexed content. [uncertain]
language_requirements: English at CEFR level B2 is required for access to the course of study. Accepted evidence: (a) an international language certification equal to or higher than B2, from the updated list of recognised certifications published by the UNIBS Language Teaching Centre (Centro Linguistico di Ateneo, CLA); (b) the CLA UNIBS B2 level certificate (attestazione CLA B2), obtained by passing the CLA level test attesting B2 in the four prescribed skills — the CLA runs preparatory training of roughly six weeks before the test; (c) having completed a previous degree delivered in English. The CLA explicitly organises English courses for students of the Master's degree in Management with the International Business and Green Economy and Sustainability curricula. Relevant CLA pages: https://www.unibs.it/en/university/organisation/language-teaching-centre-cla/cla-certification-tests-and-examination-confirmation/attestazione-di-livello-cla-lingua-inglese/attestazione-cla-b2 . The B2 requirement is identical for both English curricula of the Management LM. [uncertain] — whether a B2 certificate must already be held at application time or may be produced before matriculation could not be verified directly.

application_deadline_non_eu: Non-EU candidates residing abroad: PICA pre-assessment for master's degrees for AY 2026/2027 is open until 15 March 2026 at noon (Italian time), with outcomes notified by email around mid-May 2026; the same 15 March 2026 deadline applies to the STAR + LMINT scholarship applications. These visa/Universitaly steps are separate from, and must not be confused with, the university's own enrolment deadlines above. Non-EU candidates already legally residing in Italy follow the separate 'Non-EU candidates living in Italy: master's degrees' route. required_documents: For the PICA pre-assessment of a foreign qualification: (1) Diploma / degree certificate in the original language; (2) Transcript of records in the original language; both accompanied by an official translation into Italian or English unless already issued in one of those languages; (3) Legalisation or Apostille of the diploma and transcript by the competent authorities of the issuing education system; (4) Declaration of Value (Dichiarazione di valore) issued by the competent Italian diplomatic representation in the country of the education system attended — or an equivalent CIMEA statement of comparability where accepted; (5) detailed exam syllabi bearing the foreign university stamp and translated into Italian or English (treated by UNIBS as a preferential/recommended item); (6) proof of English at B2 (international certificate or CLA B2 attestation); (7) payment of the EUR 20 pre-assessment fee at the end of the PICA procedure; (8) valid identity document / passport. [uncertain] — whether a CV, motivation letter or CIMEA statement is formally accepted in place of the Declaration of Value for this specific course could not be verified directly.
entry_exam_or_test: Two-stage assessment rather than a single competitive exam. Stage 1 — curricular requirements: verification that the candidate has earned the minimum CFU in the SSDs listed in the Management Academic Regulations (6 CFU tolerance allowed if the disciplinary field is present). Any curricular integrations must be completed before personal preparation is assessed. Stage 2 — personal preparation: deemed satisfied without further testing if the bachelor's final mark is at least 85/110 (equivalently 77/100), or the weighted examination average is at least 23/30, or the candidate holds a GMAT total score of at least 600/800. Candidates who do not meet any of these thresholds must sit an internal admission test set by the Commission, whose topics and bibliography are published in a downloadable file on the Management enrolling page. For candidates with a foreign degree the whole verification is carried out by a dedicated Commission through the PICA pre-assessment procedure. No interview requirement distinct from the admission test was identified. [uncertain] — format, session dates and pass mark of the internal admission test could not be verified directly.

source_quotes.quote: The LM-77 Management degree is an international degree taught in English with a Curriculum in Green Economy and Sustainability and a Curriculum in International Business.

The Green Economy and Sustainability curriculum prepares students for inclusion in the company in strategic positions, General Management, new Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR)/Sustainability functions, in Marketing/Communication/PR, in Operations and Supply Chain Management, and in Administration and Control.

For candidates with a degree obtained abroad, the task of verifying admission requirements is assigned to a Commission, which verifies curricular requirements and personal preparation, deemed achieved if the candidate obtained a Bachelor's degree mark of at least 85 out of 110 (or 77 out of 100).

Personal preparation requirements are granted to students who have a weighted average of examinations of no less than 23/30 or have passed the Graduate Management Admission Test (GMAT) with a score of no less than 600/800.
Knowledge of English at least at B2 level is required for access to the course of study.
There is a 6 credits tolerance on the verification of the minimum curricular requirements, as long as the specific disciplinary field is still present.

Second Cycle Degrees run by the department of Economics and Management are open access with no limit to enrolment numbers, but registration is subject to assessment of the candidate's academic career.

For Master's degrees in Business Consultancy and Training for Professionals, Management, Money, finance and risk management for academic year 2026/2027, applications expire on August 31st, 2026 at 11:00 for preliminary assessment of eligibility criteria only or preliminary assessment and admission test; applications expire on December 31st, 2026 for directly admission applications.
The pre-assessment procedure for non-EU holders of foreign degrees aiming to enroll in Italian or English taught postgraduate degrees for 2026/2027 a.y. is open till 15 March 2026.

For open access master's degrees in Economics, Engineering and Law areas, pre-evaluation by the relevant Commission is compulsory for candidates with foreign degrees to verify if they meet specific curricular and personal preparation requirements.
The Diploma and the Transcript of records must be legalized (or bear the Apostille stamp) by authorities of the educational system they belong to.
The CLA has organized English language courses for students of the Master's degree in Management with curricula in International Business and Green Economy and Sustainability.

The Italian-language curricula include Controllo di gestione, Libera professione and Sostenibilita, as well as Finanza d'impresa, Marketing and Produzione e Logistica, while the English-language curricula include International business and Green Economy e Sustainability.
